title: Our Masala Chai, as the beach stall makes it
story: Same recipe our first stall used — strong Assam leaves, crushed ginger, and milk added only after the water boils.
steps: Boil water with ginger, cardamom, clove for 3 minutes.
Add tea leaves, simmer 2 minutes — do not boil hard.
Add milk, bring to a gentle boil, add sweetener.
Strain into a kulhad. Serve hot.

title: Cold Coffee, blended thick like the sea is still
story: We blend it with real coffee and a little vanilla so it pours like it means it. First sold to college cricketers outside RK Beach who needed the caffeine to make it to practice.
steps: Blend coffee with hot water to dissolve.
Add milk, cocoa and ice cream.
Blend 30 seconds with ice till frothy.
Pour over ice, top with ice cream if you ask nicely.

title: Mango Lassi, summer in a glass
story: Alphonso mangoes arrive from Ratnagiri in May. We churn them with curd the same day, no essence, no shortcuts.
steps: Blend mango pulp with curd and milk.
Add elaichi and sugar, blend again.
Add ice and blend till smooth.
Serve chilled with a mint leaf.

title: Mirchi Bajji, handle with respect
story: Guntur chillies are not a suggestion. Our first batch sold out in 20 minutes to stall workers who wanted heat after a cold morning.
steps: Slit chillies, remove seeds if you are brave.
Whisk besan with water, ajwain, hing and salt.
Dip chillies, fry in hot oil till golden.
Serve with onion and lemon.

title: Samosa, the 4 PM office hero
story: We fold them by hand every morning. The potato masala is meant to be a little loose so it spills out the first bite — that is the point.
steps: Knead maida with oil and salt, rest 30 min.
Temper mustard and cumin, add aloo and masala.
Roll, fill, fold into triangle, seal.
Deep fry on medium till golden.

title: Pav Bhaji that tastes like Mumbai at 7 PM
story: Butter is not optional, but the amount is your choice. Ours is generous.
steps: Melt butter, add onion and capsicum, cook soft.
Add tomato and masala, cook till jammy.
Add aloo, mash on the tawa, cook 8–10 minutes.
Serve with pav, a squeeze of lime, and more butter.

title: White Pasta, creamy without the heaviness
story: We started making white pasta for a student who only had 15 minutes before class. It became a daily special because the sauce never breaks.
steps: Boil pasta in salted water till al dente.
Melt butter, sauté garlic till fragrant.
Add flour, whisk, then milk slowly.
Toss pasta, parmesan, herbs. Serve immediately.

title: Choco Lava Cake, the warm centre we guard
story: We keep the batter at 4°C overnight so the centre stays liquid in an 8-minute bake. If your centre doesn't ooze, we replace it — no questions.
steps: Melt chocolate with butter.
Whisk eggs and sugar till pale.
Fold chocolate, flour and cocoa.
Bake 8 min at 220°C. Serve warm.

title: Sunset Sky — the one that started it all
story: We first made this at a beach shack in 2019 for a fisherman who missed sunsets because he was always fishing them in. Blue like the hour before dawn, orange like the last five minutes.
ingredients: Blue curacao syrup (or blue pea flower tea)
steps: Chill a tall glass with ice and a splash of soda.
Add pineapple and orange, stir gently.
Pour the blue curacao slowly over the back of a spoon so it layers.
Top with ginger and mint. Serve at once, before the sky changes.

title: Skyline Platter — the coastal sampler
story: Our signature small plates from across the coast — fried rice, paneer roll, and a cold drink. Built for a 4-person table that wants a bit of everything.
steps: Make fried rice with wok vegetables.
Roll paneer in paratha with chutney.
Plate both with a cold drink.
Serve on the Skyline board.
